name: Gojo
tagline: MacBook notch controls for music, windows, clipboard, files, and Night Shift

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked 2026-07-30; a three-day trial and $19.99 lifetime option are also listed.

verdictSummary: A focused notch HUD with clipboard history, a file shelf, media controls, and basic window snapping is realistic over a weekend. Matching Gojo's native polish, permission handling, local dictation, multi-display behavior, and breadth takes substantially more work.
coreLoopDIY: Hover the MacBook notch to open a local SwiftUI HUD for clipboard, files, media, windows, and display warmth.
requirements: Apple Events permission for media control
whatYouLose: signed and notarized releases with automatic updates
polished notch animations and multi-display behavior
local dictation model downloads and guarded text insertion
calendar, reminders, webcam, and battery integrations
edge-case handling across apps and macOS releases
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for a finished Mac utility that handles permissions, display quirks, updates, and several daily workflows without becoming their own maintainer.

priorArt.name: Gojo source
priorArt.desc: GPL-3.0 source for the native app, useful as implementation prior art

notes: Self-submitted by Gojo's maker; the shipped app is paid, while its source is available under GPL-3.0.
prompt:
Build me a focused macOS notch utility covering the parts of Gojo I use. Requirements:

- A native Swift 6 app for macOS 14 using SwiftUI and AppKit; generate an Xcode
  project with no third-party packages.
- Run as an accessory app with no Dock icon. Detect the built-in display notch and
  place a borderless floating panel directly below it.
- Open the panel when the pointer rests at the notch for 200 ms; close on outside
  click or Escape. Use five tabs: Music, Windows, Clipboard, Shelf, and Display.
- Clipboard: poll NSPasteboard, store the last 100 text items in Application Support,
  search them, and copy a selected item back. Ignore transient/concealed pasteboard
  types and apps in a configurable denylist.
- Shelf: accept file drops, keep security-scoped bookmarks, show file icons, and let
  me drag files back into another app. Include remove and clear-all actions.
- Music: control play/pause, previous, and next for Apple Music or Spotify through
  AppleScript, and show the active app plus track title when available.
- Windows: list visible app windows and offer left half, right half, and maximize
  actions through the Accessibility API.
- Display: save each screen's gamma table, apply blackbody RGB multipliers with
  CGSetDisplayTransferByTable, and restore the original table on disable or exit.
- Persist settings locally with UserDefaults. No accounts, cloud sync, telemetry,
  calendar, camera, dictation, battery widgets, or automatic updates.
- Include a first-run permissions screen and clear empty/error states for every tab.
- Add tests for clipboard deduplication, shelf persistence, and snap-frame math.
- README: build steps, privacy behavior, required Accessibility and Automation
  permissions, and the macOS APIs that may change between releases.
